visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: Metoclopramide, an aniline derivative with a primary aromatic amine and polar substituents, achieved absolute oral bioavailability of 79–82% in patients with cirrhosis, supporting that the query's aniline/carbamate scaffold can exceed the 20% threshold.
Bumetanide, a highly substituted aniline with multiple polar groups, had absolute oral bioavailability of 95%, further supporting high oral bioavailability for polar aniline-type structures.
The lowest L1 bioavailability value among the reference contexts is 32% for nabumetone, still above the 20% threshold; no L1 record provides affirmative evidence of F < 20%.

evidence_gaps: No direct oral bioavailability measurement is available for the query molecule itself.
All L1 records are from reference molecules rather than the exact query structure; transferability is inferred from structural and physicochemical similarity.
Solubility and first-pass metabolism of the query are not directly measured; the carbamate and aromatic amine groups could be metabolized.
No human pharmacokinetic data for the exact query structure were supplied.
content.decision_summary: Predicted high because the query has favorable physicochemical properties and all transferable L1 records report F ≥ 32%, with no affirmative evidence of F < 20%; confidence is moderate due to the absence of direct query-specific PK data.
